investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-03T01:00 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, causing a complete contract violation for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the upstream ELB endpoint that backs POST /api/agents at the /v1/agents path — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner or its configuration. All three sibling checks share the identical error message, confirming a single shared upstream dependency is the point of failure rather than any individual check's logic.

possibleCauses: Primary: The AWS ELB backing the swarm gateway in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — all three checks failed with the same 502 and ~11-second latency, consistent with a load balancer with no healthy backends or a routing failure

Secondary: A network-level connectivity issue between the production-api service and the swarm ELB (e.g., security group change, VPC routing change, or DNS resolution failure) prevented the request from reaching the ELB at all
Tertiary: The swarm gateway service itself (the process behind /v1/agents on the ELB) was crashed, restarting, or had been scaled to zero at the time of the eval run

Lower probability: A transient eval infrastructure issue caused a single run to fail — however, all three sibling checks failed with the same message and similar latencies, making a transient eval-only issue unlikely

investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-03T01:00:30–52Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at POST /api/agents before any agent identity is returned, no required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed upstream that the production-api proxies agent creation requests to at /v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents as its first step (confirmed by the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905: `createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)`), and all three checks received the same 502 response with error code "bad_gateway" and message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning". Because agent creation failed immediately, no downstream state polling or runtime checks could execute, leaving all required evidence fields empty. This is an eval-layer signal of a swarm gateway connectivity or availability problem; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals (production-api)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-03T01:00 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because the failure occurs before any agent is created, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, causing a complete contract violation for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the upstream ELB endpoint that backs POST /api/agents at the /v1/agents path — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner or its configuration. All three sibling checks share the identical error message, confirming a single shared upstream dependency is the point of failure rather than any individual check's logic.

possibleCauses: Primary: The AWS ELB backing the swarm gateway in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — all three checks failed with the same 502 and ~11-second latency, consistent with a load balancer with no healthy backends or a routing failure

Secondary: A network-level connectivity issue between the production-api service and the swarm ELB (e.g., security group change, VPC routing change, or DNS resolution failure) prevented the request from reaching the ELB at all
Tertiary: The swarm gateway service itself (the process behind /v1/agents on the ELB) was crashed, restarting, or had been scaled to zero at the time of the eval run

Lower probability: A transient eval infrastructure issue caused a single run to fail — however, all three sibling checks failed with the same message and similar latencies, making a transient eval-only issue unlikely

affectedAreas.reason: This is the API surface that proxies to the swarm gateway. It returned 502 bad_gateway for all three eval attempts, blocking agent creation entirely.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All checks under the remote-agents feature (features.json lines 183-185) failed with the identical error, indicating the shared upstream dependency (swarm gateway) is the blast radius.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote-agent-runtime probe branch
affectedAreas.reason: The probe at line 1913-1918 calls createAgent as its first step; a 502 at that call prevents all evidence collection and causes the expected-output contract to be entirely unmet.

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: Contract at lines 266-270 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message; zero fields were collected because the gateway failure prevented agent creation.

recommendedNextActions: Check AWS ELB target group health and CloudWatch metrics for the swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 at 2026-09-03T01:00Z to determine whether the gateway was down, draining, or had no healthy targets.

Review production-api server logs for POST /api/agents 502 errors at the same timestamp to determine the scope of impact (eval-only vs. broader traffic) and whether the error originated from a connection failure or an application-level rejection.
Re-run the three remote-agents evals now to determine if the gateway has recovered and the failure was transient.
If the gateway is confirmed down or degraded, engage the team responsible for the swarm gateway infrastructure to investigate the ELB and its target group in us-east-2.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false in features.json (line 185), so this check alone does not trigger a feature outage classification; however, the required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) are marked required=true and their failure does breach the degradedAfterFailures=1 threshold for the remote-agents feature.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the swarm gateway has recovered. A pass would confirm a transient outage; a continued 502 would indicate a persistent gateway or routing problem.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared dependency failure pattern persists across all three checks or has become isolated to one, helping localize the fault boundary.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect AWS ELB target group health for the swarm gateway in us-east-2 around 2026-09-03T01:00Z
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: CloudWatch metrics and ELB access logs would confirm whether the gateway had unhealthy targets, a deployment event, or a network-level connectivity failure at the time of the eval run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check production-api logs for 502 errors on POST /api/agents around 2026-09-03T01:00Z
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Server-side logs would show whether the 502 was returned for all callers (gateway-wide outage) or only for the eval probe's requests (credential, quota, or routing issue specific to the probe identity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful POST /api/agents response (2xx) from the production-api at the same timestamp would disprove that the swarm gateway was down.
ELB access logs showing healthy target responses and no 5xx errors around 2026-09-03T01:00Z would indicate the failure was not at the gateway layer.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state at the same timestamp would disprove that the swarm gateway was the shared dependency failure.
Evidence that the 502 is returned only for the eval probe's credentials or org context (e.g., a quota or auth error surfaced as 502) would shift the cause away from gateway availability.

A prior history of passing runs immediately before this timestamp would help distinguish a transient outage from a persistent misconfiguration; the absence of any lastPassingAt value (null) means this cannot currently be ruled out as a first-time or persistent failure.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated swarm-gateway-health eval that directly probes the ELB /v1/agents endpoint health check path (if one exists) independently of the full agent provisioning flow, to distinguish gateway availability from API-layer failures earlier.

Add a gateway-reachability pre-check step to the remote-agent-create probe that emits a structured evidence field (e.g., gatewayReachable: true/false) before attempting full provisioning, so future failures can be localized to the gateway vs. the provisioning logic.
Introduce historical run tracking for the remote-agents checks so that lastPassingAt is populated; this would allow future investigations to distinguish transient outages from persistent regressions.

Consider adding a latency-band assertion to the remote-agent-create contract: the ~11 s failure latency is consistent with a TCP connect timeout and could be flagged as a warning-level signal before a full 502 is returned.
